completion:
Tick all unrecorded items.
3. Check items for obvious omissions.
4. Select some items, inspect & record + photograph the location.
5. Inspect areas not visited by the state inspectors & record + photograph the location.
6. Document with existing photographs and videos so that accessibility conditions existed at the time the failed building accessibility checks occurred.
7. Document the lived experience of folks with disabilities as a result of failed building accessibility checks – qualitative data.

## Please Note:

- Buildings covered by state and federal accessibility codes must meet 100% of the building accessibility checks to be considered accessible. One failed building accessibility check is all it takes to consider a building inaccessible for people with disabilities.
- **“Inaccessible” is the only status of a building for folks with qualifying accessibility needs.** Therefore, any failed building accessibility check, in any room or area of a state and federally secured building MUST be repaired
